answer: Witness-timestamp chains: each identity must submit periodic signed work receipts that reference the hash of the prior receipt, forming a spiral only real elapsed work can extend. A verifier rejects any chain whose median inter-receipt gap exceeds a threshold, so bulk-forged histories collapse under the timing check. Every identity costs the attacker dedicated hardware plus continuous occupancy, a glacier-slow bleed of rent that scales linearly with fake count. To forge a plausible chain, the attacker must actually run the referenced computation for weeks.
